statement: ORB (09:30 ET basic breakout) stitched walk-forward OOS performance is materially better on 6E and GC than on ES and NQ (claim from prior ORB research).
test_plan: Compare stitched OOS mean R, t-stat and PF of primary_12_3_3 per instrument; then lockbox.

statement: Opening ranges of 10-20 minutes outperform 5-minute ranges out of sample.
test_plan: OOS phase heatmaps Range x R/TF and range chosen by WFO; neighbour plateau check.

statement: For 6E and GC the most robust target lies below 2R (0.75R-1.5R region forms an OOS plateau).
test_plan: OOS phase heatmap Range x R and Stop x R; plateau classification of WFO selections.

statement: The simple close-confirmed basic breakout performs at least as well OOS as limit-retrace and stop-order entries after realistic costs.
test_plan: Family-restricted WFO (market/limit/stop) stitched OOS with slippage sensitivity.

statement: Most of any ORB edge occurs with entries shortly after the open; expectancy declines with later cutoffs.
test_plan: OOS heatmap R x Cutoff; OOS trades bucketed by entry time.

statement: The ORB phenomenon is specific to the 09:30 U.S. cash open: start times 09:00/09:15/09:45/10:00 perform worse OOS.
test_plan: real_start_time WFO after the 09:30 study is complete.

note: Registered before any real market data was loaded.
